annotations.text:
INSTRUMENT — seven screens from one system

Read the sheet on the left first. Every screen to the right is assembled from it and adds nothing: the same 56px row, the same four sizes, the same two faces, the same 8% hairline. There is not one card, shadow or rounded panel in the whole set.

That is the test of a direction. If a new screen needs a new component, either the screen is wrong or the system is incomplete — and so far neither has been.

WHERE THE ARC IS ALLOWED

Twice in the app, and both times it is the subject: charge on the dashboard, session progress on charging. Anywhere else it would be ornament pretending to be an instrument.

The garage is the proof it scales: at 46px the same arc becomes a row ornament that still carries the number, so two cars read at a glance without a second component being invented for them.

What it deliberately does NOT do: the trip screen has four charging stops and no arcs at all — a route is a sequence, so it gets a spine and per-stop SOC bars. Costs has bars, because money over time is a comparison, not a level. Using the arc there would have been style over meaning.

WHAT I AM STILL UNSURE ABOUT

· The arc reads a level, not a difference. 24% and 27% look the same. If precision matters more than character, the dashboard hero becomes a bar and the direction survives — the arc is the most replaceable part of it.

· Space Grotesk 300 at 64px+ is thin. It holds on an OLED phone in shade; in direct sun it may need 400. That is a decision to make on a real screen outdoors, not here.

· Rows with no fill rely entirely on the 8% hairline for structure. On a cheap panel with a blue-light filter that hairline can disappear. Worth testing before committing.

Not yet drawn in this language: documents, insights, energy, settings, debug. They are all list screens and derive directly from the row — but I have not drawn them, so I am not claiming they are done.

THE TWO I DID NOT TAKE

Kept because the choice should stay visible, and because either could be re-skinned onto the same structure if you prefer it. Their tradeoffs are unchanged: Editorial costs real tappability on a phone, Ambient looks like everything else shipping right now.

TODAY, AND THE TARGETED FIXES

These are defects, not taste — the car-asleep state that deletes the screen, commands the car will refuse being offered confidently, the walking distance set at 11px grey.

Worth shipping whichever direction wins, and cheaper to ship before a redesign than during one.
